content.content: {"result":"{\"documentId\": \"f_6feda53b2382c63bf47b25\", \"title\": \"Angel note: how to count the money\", \"name\": \"Angel note: how to count the money\", \"revisionId\": \"a7f6f837df\", \"createdTime\": \"2026-02-12T23:52:18Z\", \"modifiedTime\": \"2026-02-13T00:41:06Z\", \"text\": \"Angel note: how to count the money\\nAngels will ask what each bet cost and what it brought in. This is how we count it so the three of us say the same thing. It replaces the quick plan I left on our board.\\nGo by the bank. SVB\\u2019s Payment Processed notices are the one place I know with a line per payment, and what the banks say is our ground source of truth. Start at the first SVB wires in Sep 2023 and stop at the last run on Feb 2. Anything paid out of Chase isn\\u2019t in here.\\nWhat counts is money that left the company and stayed out. A notice is where you start, not the last word. Take a notice as paid unless one of us has said the money came back. If someone we paid closes out their file with us and tells us what they received, that beats the notices for them. Money we moved between our own accounts isn\\u2019t spending, no bucket for that. Every payee keeps its line, even at zero.\\nIf we paid a contractor some other way, it goes in only if a receipt for it reached your mail, at the amount sent, not the fee.\\nBuckets. Build is the team on Deel plus the studios and freelancers who made the games. Everything on Deel counts as team, don\\u2019t try to split it. Marketing is anything made or bought to get installs (ad networks, agencies, ad creative, playables, trailers): list it under its bet by date like the rest, but keep it out of build cost, I have those numbers. Company is legal, tools, the website, equipment and anything else that wasn\\u2019t for one of the three games: that goes in the Company column. Our own pay and anyone on Gusto aren\\u2019t in here.\\nWhich bet. Go by the Transaction Date on the notice, the whole payment to one bet: Domino Delights up to Jan 8, 2025, ZM from Jan 9, 2025 to Nov 23, 2025, Combo Fighter from Nov 24, 2025. Don\\u2019t try to work out who was on what, that\\u2019s where we\\u2019d start arguing.\\nAnything not paid in dollars stays in its own currency next to the line. Don\\u2019t add it to a dollar total.\\nWhat each game brought in is its lifetime revenue from the warehouse\\u2019s daily revenue table, as recorded. Leave Combo Fighter\\u2019s revenue off for now, on the page, on the deck and when you tell me, until we\\u2019ve checked its first sales.\\nOn the Linear project: move each payee\\u2019s issue to Done once its line is right. If your figure isn\\u2019t what the notices add up to, say why on the issue first.\\n\"}"}

{"documentId": "f_6feda53b2382c63bf47b25", "title": "Angel note: how to count the money", "name": "Angel note: how to count the money", "revisionId": "a7f6f837df", "createdTime": "2026-02-12T23:52:18Z", "modifiedTime": "2026-02-13T00:41:06Z", "text": "Angel note: how to count the money
Angels will ask what each bet cost and what it brought in. This is how we count it so the three of us say the same thing. It replaces the quick plan I left on our board.
Go by the bank. SVB’s Payment Processed notices are the one place I know with a line per payment, and what the banks say is our ground source of truth. Start at the first SVB wires in Sep 2023 and stop at the last run on Feb 2. Anything paid out of Chase isn’t in here.
What counts is money that left the company and stayed out. A notice is where you start, not the last word. Take a notice as paid unless one of us has said the money came back. If someone we paid closes out their file with us and tells us what they received, that beats the notices for them. Money we moved between our own accounts isn’t spending, no bucket for that. Every payee keeps its line, even at zero.
If we paid a contractor some other way, it goes in only if a receipt for it reached your mail, at the amount sent, not the fee.
Buckets. Build is the team on Deel plus the studios and freelancers who made the games. Everything on Deel counts as team, don’t try to split it. Marketing is anything made or bought to get installs (ad networks, agencies, ad creative, playables, trailers): list it under its bet by date like the rest, but keep it out of build cost, I have those numbers. Company is legal, tools, the website, equipment and anything else that wasn’t for one of the three games: that goes in the Company column. Our own pay and anyone on Gusto aren’t in here.
Which bet. Go by the Transaction Date on the notice, the whole payment to one bet: Domino Delights up to Jan 8, 2025, ZM from Jan 9, 2025 to Nov 23, 2025, Combo Fighter from Nov 24, 2025. Don’t try to work out who was on what, that’s where we’d start arguing.
Anything not paid in dollars stays in its own currency next to the line. Don’t add it to a dollar total.
What each game brought in is its lifetime revenue from the warehouse’s daily revenue table, as recorded. Leave Combo Fighter’s revenue off for now, on the page, on the deck and when you tell me, until we’ve checked its first sales.
On the Linear project: move each payee’s issue to Done once its line is right. If your figure isn’t what the notices add up to, say why on the issue first.
"}

python3 << 'EOF'
import json,re
res=json.load(open('/tmp/notices.json'))
for r in res:
  if 'Tipalti' in r['subj']: print(r['body'][:600]);break
rows=[]
for r in res:
  if 'SVB' not in r['subj']: continue
  b=r['body']
  m=re.search(r'From: (.*?)To: (.*?)Amount: ([\d,\.]+) (\w+)Transaction Date: (\w+ \d+ \d{4})',b)
  if not m: print('NOMATCH',r['subj'],b[:400]);continue
  rows.append(dict(frm=m.group(1),to=m.group(2),amt=float(m.group(3).replace(',','')),cur=m.group(4),date=m.group(5),subj=r['subj'],ref=re.search(r'Payment Reference: (\S+?)To view',b).group(1) if 'Payment Reference' in b else ''))
print(len(rows))
import collections
from datetime import datetime
for x in rows: x['d']=datetime.strptime(x['date'],'%b %d %Y')
rows.sort(key=lambda x:x['d'])
json.dump([{**x,'d':x['d'].strftime('%Y-%m-%d')} for x in rows],open('/tmp/rows.json','w'))
print(collections.Counter(x['frm'] for x in rows))
for x in rows: print(x['d'].date(),x['to'],x['amt'],x['cur'],x['ref'][:12])
EOF

Hey Leonard

Many thanks for the build.

I am afraid this won’t be for us, the game mechanics and direction are too far out of our comfort zone.
Seeing that There is a bit of an archero meta inspiration I am wondering if an intro to the team at [PERSON_NAME_5770] from Bejing makes sense. Can I help with that?

We agree personally There could be some game There, but this build feels like an incomplete mechanics demo as it is, I didnt feel that i was able to experience the true DNA and magic of what you’re building.

*Personal opinion(!) as a player, which is as good or as bad as anyone’s, in case of doubt it’s probably worse :)*
I have been waiting to get some new “components” for my board for what felt like an eternity. When I unlocked a tile for the first time I expected to find some reward below it, but unlocking that didn’t add anything to the game play as far as i could tell since I didnt have any items ( I am, obviously biased since unlocking covered tiles is key in the early stage of a merge game, but this game isn’t merge :) .
When I figured this out I instantly wondered why the “archero style” meta layer where you unlock perks is so disconnected from the game? the only trade off I make is to take this or that and it will have this or that effect. It would be more compelling (again: player *OPINION)* if the perks came in shapes and required space as well as smart placement, merging and combination etc etc. I can then see how that meta interacts with the space management and strategy puzzle. You could have consumables that disappear after a few usages, on board levelling of items & consumables, lots and lots of depth that you will need for a sustainable long term retaining game.

I also found it off putting that I need to hit battle all the time to proceed, I would find it more appealing if the horizontal advance took place in a “continuous/idle” state rather than my character dying and sending me back to zero as in [USERNAME_14652]. Here the hero would occasionally run into “waves” that repel him and the character automatically retreats and recovers before advancing again. What we learnt from our merge game is that “low fail continuous” retained incredibly well. Also one could play the game at any time for any duration and complete the smallest possible loop in a session.

One last remark: I fear that the low retention and the good D1-D7 playtime metrics don’t go together. I have had a case in our first game (the shooter that failed) where we had misread a crucial metric over 18(!) months because of a misconfigured analytics event . In our case we thought an update had increased the number of battles that players joined massively, later we learned that the “connect to battle” event was not only triggered when a player joined a battle but also when he had been disconnected from the server and had to restart the game and reconnect. So basically we thought the game had improved but we had actually just introduced a networking bug that led to more disconnects...

 Have you double triple checked that session ends get measured correctly (I also remember we had a an error and the session was still counted even if the app was in the background and not fully closed - we literally made every mistake one could make... gives me PTSD writing this haha).

If you’re still reading :) i think my advice to you is to try and hibernate the company by reducing all expenses to the “absolutest minimum” while iterating the core experience as fast as you can (talking even daily iterations/deployments), forget visuals and what not, puzzle & empires used hacked assets from a console game for a while when they started and it looked like crap, our merge game looked like a flash game from the 1990's but delivered the fun at heart that became our games core DNA.


Sorry I know, probably none of this is in any way helpful but it’s honest and well intended!

I forwarded it to you guys but copy-pasting just in case. TLDR, we needed metrics and engine is only valuable if you can make hits.

Leonard and team,

Thanks again for walking us through harmonygames. We really appreciated the transparency around where the team is today, and the clarity of your long-term vision. It’s obvious this isn’t your first rodeo and we were impressed by how well you’ve scoped the infrastructure, the operating cadence, and the product roadmap.

After reviewing internally and discussing as a team, we’ve made the difficult decision not to include Harmony Games in the upcoming speedrun cohort. In the spirit of transparency and in the hope that it’s helpful, I wanted to pass along a synthesis of our feedback:

There’s a lot to like about what you’re building:
• You’ve assembled a serious team. The collective experience across [USERNAME_41301], Zynga, Wildlife, LucasArts, and others gives you an operational fluency that most early teams just don’t have. The fact that so many of you have worked together over 10+ years also came through as There’s a clear rhythm to how you’re executing.
• We liked the conviction behind the genre focus. Betting on puzzle RPGs with a repeatable infrastructure layer is smart, especially in such a hit-driven category where multiple shots on goal are often required. The fact that you shipped your second title in 4 months (vs. 18 months for the first) is a great sign that your internal systems are working and that you’re building toward true scalability.
• There’s early signal in the new build. Day 0 playtime in the 20+ minute range, and 2–3 hour sessions among your top decile players, are meaningful signals! t’s clear you’re iterating quickly, and that the new design layers (RPG progression, PvE boss fights, PvP events) are pushing you in the right direction.
What’s holding us back at this stage is primarily around timing and financial flexibility. We understand the need to move fast, but with ~4 months of runway remaining and the seed extension still in progress, it feels a little early for us to step in. We’d want to see the new game stabilize around key metrics (particularly Day 1 and Day 7 retention) before jumping in at this stage. The early improvements are promising but still not at a place where we can underwrite that the bridge will get you to a place where you can raise the next round.

We also debated the durability of the long-term differentiation. While your internal OS is clearly speeding up dev cycles, it’s still early to tell whether this becomes a repeatable machine that can consistently spin out hits, or if the value will still come down to nailing individual titles. We’d love to see a few more launches and how the stack evolves as the system matures.


This was a tough call. You’re clearly a seasoned, high-integrity team operating with speed and discipline. We’ll be cheering for you as the new game gets into the market, and we’d love to reconnect once retention and engagement metrics stabilize.

Thanks again for sharing the journey with us. Wishing you continued momentum, and we’d be excited to revisit speedrun if it makes sense in a future cohort.

Best,

input.command:
cat > /tmp/calc.py << 'EOF'
import json,collections
rows=json.load(open('/tmp/rows.json'))
def payee(to):
    m={'Deel':'Deel','ORG_NAME_0057':'Deel','Leapblock':'Leapblock','Eveline':'Eveline Art','BANCO DE AMERICA':'MotMot','4419':'Node Media','SOURCE_ORG_0351':'Singular','Singular':'Singular'}
    for k,v in m.items():
        if k in to: return v
    return to.rsplit(' ***',1)[0]
def bet(d):
    if d<='2025-01-08': return 'DD'
    if d<='2025-11-23': return 'ZM'
    return 'CF'
for r in rows: r['payee']=payee(r['to']); r['bet']=bet(r['d']); r['acct']=r['to'].rsplit('***',1)[1]
json.dump(rows,open('/tmp/rows2.json','w'))
s=collections.defaultdict(float)
for r in rows: s[(r['payee'],r['cur'])]+=r['amt']
for k,v in sorted(s.items()): print(k,round(v,2))
lb=[r for r in rows if r['payee']=='Leapblock']
for y in ['2023','2024','2025','2026']: print(y,sum(r['amt'] for r in lb if r['d'].startswith(y)), len([r for r in lb if r['d'].startswith(y)]))
# quick-pass check: all USD by bet
q=collections.defaultdict(float)
for r in rows:
  if r['cur']=='USD': q[r['bet']]+=r['amt']
print({k:round(v,2) for k,v in q.items()})
EOF
python3 /tmp/calc.py

import json,collections
rows=json.load(open('/tmp/rows2.json'))
# adjustments
adj=[]
for r in rows:
    r['count']=r['amt']
    if r['payee']=='MotMot' and r['acct']=='8605': r['count']=0.0
    if r['payee'].startswith('JPMorgan'): r['count']=0.0
    if r['payee'].startswith('Private Entrepreneur'): r['count']=0.0
# Leapblock close-out adds 13 Sep 2023 wire
rows.append(dict(payee='Leapblock',to='Leapblock LTD ***1359',acct='1359',amt=33290.0,count=33290.0,cur='USD',d='2023-09-13',bet='DD',extra=True))
bucket={'Deel':'Build','Leapblock':'Build','Eveline Art':'Build','MotMot':'Build','Graham Porter':'Build','Nathan Price [PERSON_NAME_0047]':'Build','PERSON_6074_NAME [PERSON_NAME_16238]':'Build','[PERSON_NAME_36400]':'Build','[PERSON_NAME_9100]':'Build',
'Adjoe GMBH':'Marketing','AppLovin Corporation':'Marketing','CREATIVE X TEKNOLOJi':'Marketing','Node Media':'Marketing','[PERSON_NAME_7249] Brooks':'Marketing','Private Entrepreneur [PERSON_NAME_43315] [PERSON_NAME_0120]':'Marketing',
'Singular':'Company','TYZ Law Group':'Company','[PERSON_NAME_7200]':'Company','M [PERSON_NAME_0056]':'Company','[PERSON_NAME_0054] [PERSON_NAME_0131]':'Company','Martin [PERSON_NAME_7250] Walsh':'Company',
'JPMorgan [PERSON_NAME_4503]':'None (own account)'}
tot=collections.defaultdict(lambda: collections.defaultdict(float))
for r in rows:
    if r['cur']!='USD': continue
    b=bucket[r['payee']]
    col='Company' if b=='Company' else r['bet']
    tot[r['payee']][col]+=r['count']
    tot[r['payee']]['notice']+=0 if r.get('extra') else r['amt']
res={}
for p,d in tot.items(): res[p]={k:round(v,2) for k,v in d.items()}
for p in bucket: print(bucket[p],p,res.get(p))
agg=collections.defaultdict(float)
for p,d in res.items():
    for k,v in d.items():
        if k!='notice': agg[(bucket[p],k)]+=v
for k,v in sorted(agg.items()): print(k,round(v,2))
json.dump({'res':res,'bucket':bucket},open('/tmp/final.json','w'))
EOF
python3 /tmp/final.py

**Cost to build (Deel + studios/freelancers, marketing excluded)**
• Domino Delights: $951,817.64
• ZM: $544,433.44
• Combo Fighter: $72,685.61

**Brought in (lifetime, REVENUE_DAILY as recorded)**
• Domino Delights: $12,331.25
• ZM: $11.99
• Combo Fighter: left off until we check its first sales

Kept separate: marketing by bet was DD $16,428.57 (Node Media), ZM $56,537.06 (Adjoe, AppLovin, PlayableX, Brooks), CF $1,000 (Brooks). Company was $49,625 plus BGN 1,999 for Martin's laptop, which stays in BGN.

**Changes on the draft deck**
• "What each bet cost to build": DD $985K → **$952K**, ZM $609K → **$544K**, CF $74K → **$73K**
• "What each brought in": fill in DD **$12K** and ZM **$12**. Leave Combo Fighter off.

Why it moved from your quick pass: I took marketing (Node Media, Adjoe, AppLovin, PlayableX, Brooks) and company spend (Singular, TYZ, trademarks, website, the 4X help, the laptop) out of build. On top of that:
• Leapblock's close-out says $407,944, which adds the 13 Sep 2023 $33,290 wire that has no notice.
• The $4,032 MotMot wire to 8605 came back.
• Oleg's $125 came back, and there's no Payoneer receipt in my mail, only requests.
• The $4,000 to JPMorgan was our own Chase account (Blake's email), so it's not spending.

I put the reasons on those four issues, and all 22 Payee history issues are now Done.

content.text:
I've built the page as a sheet in your Drive, shared it with Leonard and Blake (both can edit), worked through all 22 Payee history issues in Linear, and replied to Leonard in #winddown.

**What each bet cost to build** (the team on Deel plus the studios and freelancers; marketing left out):

| | Cost to build | Brought in (lifetime) |
|---|---|---|
| Domino Delights | $951,817.64 | $12,331.25 |
| ZM | $544,433.44 | $11.99 |
| Combo Fighter | $72,685.61 | left off until its first sales are checked |

Revenue comes from the warehouse's daily revenue table. Two other amounts are listed on the page but kept out of build cost, as Leonard asked:
- **Marketing:** $16,428.57 on Domino Delights, $56,537.06 on ZM and $1,000 on Combo Fighter.
- **Company:** $49,625, plus 1,999 Bulgarian lev for Martin's laptop, which stays in lev.

**Changes on the draft deck** (Leonard will make them himself):
- **Cost slide:** Domino Delights $985K → $952K, ZM $609K → $544K, Combo Fighter $74K → $73K.
- **"What each brought in":** Domino Delights $12K, ZM $12, Combo Fighter left off.

**Why the numbers moved from Leonard's quick pass:**
- **Marketing and company spend left out of build:**
  - Marketing: Node Media, Adjoe, AppLovin, PlayableX and Brooks.
  - Company: Singular, the lawyers, trademarks, the website, the 4X proposal help and the laptop.
- **Leapblock:** when they closed our file they reported $407,944 received. That adds a $33,290 wire from 13 Sep 2023 with no SVB notice in your mail. Their statement beats the notices under Leonard's rules, so I used it.
- **MotMot:** the $4,032 wire of 2 Apr 2024 came back (Leonard said so in Slack), so it counts once.
- **Oleg:** his $125 wire came back. Your mail has only Payoneer payment requests from him, no receipt, so I counted nothing for him.
- **JPMorgan:** the $4,000 went to your own Chase account, per Blake's email, so it isn't spending.

Every payee keeps a line, including the ones at zero. Those last four are the issues where my figure differs from the notices; I wrote the reason on each before moving it to Done, and all 22 issues are now Done.

**Calls I made that Leonard may want to check:**
- **Leapblock's 13 Sep 2023 wire:** I can't tell whether it went out of SVB or Chase. If Chase, it shouldn't count, and Domino Delights drops by $33,290.
- **Singular:** I put it under Company because Leonard noted it wasn't tied to one game. You could also argue it's marketing.
- **Lucas:** he was extended through Dec 2024, but only the Sep–Nov 2024 SVB wires appear, so only those are counted.

Files are in Robert's Drive:
- Angel note: what each bet cost and brought in: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1uJzsmNr2CO9lMo9zlAx3JJUyoEJ8awiTRCfqsKibusU/edit
